text.p: Five weeks after pitching a no-hitter, Kevin Brown limited Los Angeles to one hit as the Florida Marlins defeated the Dodgers, 5-1, on Wednesday.
Brown (9-6) allowed only Raul Mondesi's fifth-inning single. He walked one and struck out eight in improving to 3-1 lifetime against the Dodgers.

"I felt great tonight, I'm happy with the results," said Brown, who retired the first 10 batters and the last 15. This was his fourth complete game and first since throwing a no-hitter at San Francisco on June 10.

"My ball wasn't moving well, so all I tried to do was hit the corners," Brown said. "But it's like the old saying goes, 'Just win, baby.' It was not a night where I felt that I could be dominant. But it's a funny thing in this game, you can have great stuff and lose or you can have lousy stuff and win."
Edgar Renterio had three hits, including a two-run triple in the sixth inning, for the Marlins.

In Atlanta, Chipper Jones snapped an eighth-inning tie with a one-out RBI single, and Tom Glavine and Mark Wohlers combined on a five-hitter as the Braves dealt the Colorado Rockies their fifth straight loss, 2-1.
Jones, batting .500 (24-for-48) during a 12-game hitting streak, laced a 2-1 pitch from reliever Jerry DiPoto (3-2) up the middle, scoring Michael Tucker, who had doubled.

Glavine (10-5) allowed one run and five hits over eight innings with three walks and five strikeouts. He also had two hits to raise his average to .237. Wohlers struck out two in a perfect ninth for his 23rd save in 25 opportunities.

In Houston, Mike Hampton tossed a four-hitter for his third complete game in four starts and Jeff Bagwell had two hits and three RBI, leading the Astros to their third straight win, an 8-1 romp over the San Francisco Giants.
The victory lifted Houston into a first-place tie with Pittsburgh in the National League Central.

Hampton (6-7) won his third straight decision, limiting the Giants to three singles and a double with no walks and five strikeouts. He improved to 3-0 this month with a 1.69 ERA and helped the Astros move over the .500 mark for the first time since May 25.

In New York, rookie Jeremi Gonzalez survived five rocky innings to win his fifth straight game and Sammy Sosa and Scott Servais made key defensive plays, enabling the Chicago Cubs to edge the Mets, 6-5.
Gonzalez (7-2) allowed five runs and three hits in five innings, walking five. Four relievers then combined for four scoreless innings, with Mel Rojas earning his 10th save.
The Mets have dropped three straight games, each by one run, and four of their last five.

In Philadelphia, Curt Schilling fired a four-hitter and Scott Rolen had a homer and an RBI single as the Phillies won consecutive games for the first time since May with a 6-0 victory over the Montreal Expos.

Schilling (11-8) didn't walk a batter and struck out seven to record his fourth complete game and first shutout of the season while increasing his league-leading strikeout total to 176. It was his ninth career shutout.
Schilling retired 21 of the last 23 batters and went to more than one ball on a batter just three times.
In Pittsburgh, newly-acquired Jon Nunnally homered and drove in three runs and Dave Burba scattered eight hits for his second complete game as the Cincinnati Reds cooled off the Pirates, 7-3.

Nunnally, acquired Tuesday in a four-player deal with the Kansas City Royals, made his first start for the Reds. He had a sacrifice fly in a three-run first inning and belted a two-run homer in the fifth.

In St. Louis, Ken Caminiti's two-out single in the top of the ninth inning scored Rickey Henderson with the go-ahead run, enabling the San Diego Padres to beat the Cardinals, 4-3, for their fourth win in five games.

With one out in the ninth, Henderson singled to right off T.J. Mathews (4-4). He stole second and moved to third when Quilvio Veras grounded to Mathews, who tagged Veras. Tony Gwynn walked before Caminiti lined an 0-1 pitch to centre field to break a 3-3 tie.
